findings.title: Workstation path and username in committed doc
findings.problem: The committed technical analysis names the reviewer's absolute workstation path, including the local OS username, as its Workspace line, plus a local commit reference. Source: blind.
findings.impact: Personal and environment details of a developer land in the repository history of a published project; the line is confirmed present at HEAD.
findings.recommendation: Replace the absolute workspace path with a repository-relative reference (e.g. `codemie-code` @ `<commit>`), and drop the local OS username from every committed story artifact.
findings.check_notes: HEAD technical-analysis.md:6 reads repository `codemie-code` @ fc983e00; no /Users/, /home/ or username in the story/spec dirs

findings.title: Over-limit files grow past 500 lines

Source: standards.
findings.impact: code-quality is a blocking standard of this repository and no automated gate enforces the file-size rule; the change moves three files further past the documented limit.

What this change adds to them is the wiring at their own seams (the sync commands' options, the adapter's type members, the plugin's hook members); every new file of the change is under 500 lines, and the two files the change itself had pushed over the limit were split. Moving the existing commands out of these files is a refactoring of code this change does not otherwise touch.

findings.title: Mode resolved below process entries (D3)
findings.problem: D3 requires the modes to be told apart once per process, at its entry, with no 'if local' branch below. The collection is also resolved inside ProxyCheck.run (ProxyCheck.ts:21) and inside the Claude plugin's pre-spawn refresh (claude.plugin.ts:630, stated as deliberate in the PR), and backend code branches on the mode: adoptLiveDaemon has `if (state.mode === 'local') return false;` (otlp-cold-start.ts:139). Source: acceptance.
findings.impact: An approved design decision is only partly met; each placement has a plausible reason (a doctor check, a launcher refresh, refusing to adopt a foreign local daemon), so whether they are acceptable exceptions needs the story owner's intent.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether D3 admits these three placements: resolveCollection() inside ProxyCheck.run (src/cli/commands/doctor/checks/ProxyCheck.ts:21), inside the Claude plugin's pre-spawn refresh (src/agents/plugins/claude/claude.plugin.ts:630), and the `state.mode === 'local'` branch in backend adoptLiveDaemon (src/cli/commands/proxy/otlp-cold-start.ts:139). Either record them as accepted exceptions in the story's D3, or pass the resolved collection in from the process entry and expose the daemon's adoptability through the collection instead of a mode check.
findings.check_notes: decision mapped with outcome and rationale; ProxyCheck.ts no longer calls resolveCollection, doctor/index.ts:95 resolves once

decision.outcome: decided by the story owner: one placement fixed in the fix-up commit 1f0e1361, D3 restated for the other two
decision.rationale: `codemie doctor` now resolves the collection once in its action, before it builds its checks, and hands the doctor plan to ProxyCheck (src/cli/commands/doctor/index.ts, checks/ProxyCheck.ts takes the plan; it calls no resolveCollection). D3 of the story and of the spec now states the rule as the code keeps it: the modes are told apart once per process — at the command's entry; in an agent launcher, which has no command entry of its own for the analytics, at the one place before the client is spawned (carrying the collection through the launcher shared by every agent would change all of them for one caller); after that nothing branches on this process's mode. The check in adoptLiveDaemon reads what ANOTHER process's daemon is, as the same function reads that daemon's version: it is not a branch on this process's mode.

findings.title: scope-disabled left out of filter reasons
findings.problem: COPILOT_FILTER_REASONS holds analytics-disabled, project-excluded and scope-untracked but not scope-disabled, while Claude's FILTER_REASONS includes disabled. A Copilot hook refused as scope-disabled never writes an exclusion mark. Source: blind.
findings.impact: Only matters if scope-disabled is meant as a developer filter; trigger is a connector scope record with enabled=false on a local machine, which the local install itself writes enabled.
findings.recommendation: Question: is scope-disabled deliberately not a developer filter (connector never enabled)? If so, say so in the COPILOT_FILTER_REASONS comment; if not, add it.

findings.title: Git target keeps stale same-day part files
findings.problem: The OTLP file name depends on the run's part count (`part-k-of-n`, or no part suffix for one file), and GitTarget.deliver only writes files (git-target.ts:93) without removing the day's earlier set. Source: edge.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger: two runs on the same UTC day whose part count differs (a multi-part export needs more than 70 MB gzipped) leave an earlier set next to the new one; line ids keep the overlap deduplicable.
findings.recommendation: Before writing, remove this developer's existing `codemie-analytics-<slug>-<date>*.otlp.jsonl.gz` files for the run date in the git working copy.

findings.title: Uninstall drops spool sessions still in grace
findings.problem: teardown removes localSpoolRoot() after resolveMarkers() without a final sweep, so sessions still inside their 15/60-minute grace are deleted and never reach the analytics folder. AC16 only requires the already-stored sessions to stay. Source: edge.
findings.impact: Sessions active within the last hour before uninstall are lost; workaround is to wait an hour after the last session before uninstalling.
findings.recommendation: Question: is dropping not-yet-finished spool sessions on uninstall intended? If not, run sweepToFolder() ignoring grace before removing the spool.

findings.title: Folder build failure also blocks JSON report
findings.problem: LocalExportSource.build awaits the OTLP folder build before the JSON report with no catch, so any throw from OtlpFolderSource (an oversized single line, EACCES on a folder file) aborts the JSON report too. Source: edge.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger (a single line over the gzip cap, or an unreadable file in the 0o700 folder), but then D20's JSON report is not delivered either, on every later run while the cause persists.
findings.recommendation: Build the JSON report independently of the folder build (e.g. Promise.allSettled), deliver what succeeded and report the folder failure separately, without moving the OTLP marker.

findings.title: Resumed move ignores a later exclusion mark
findings.problem: resumeMove copies and finishes a marked session without checking isSessionExcluded, while startMove (analytics-folder.ts:253) drops excluded sessions. Source: edge.
findings.impact: Reachability unconfirmed: needs a move interrupted after its marker was written and a hook from that session firing in an excluded folder before the next sweep; only lines up to the marker's bounds are copied.
findings.recommendation: In resumeMove, when isSessionExcluded(sessionId), cut the folder back to the marker lengths, delete the spool session and remove the marker instead of copying.
